answer: Slot congestion toll: at dawn, every agent must commit to a time slot. An agent's fee for a slot equals the current number of commitments already in that slot, so the k-th commitment costs k-1. A sparrow of sybils that all choose the same time slot pays 0+1+...+(m-1) for m identities. The cost scales with the size of the dune they form, making coordination itself the priced resource.
